(name lost) for its maintenance; Dindha, son of... and Nizām, son of Nașīr, cleared the mud from the date of this deed they were permitted to grow the kharif and rabi crops and sow whatever they liked. The last lines are imprecatory. Also mentions Nizām Attah, son of Maulānā Khwāja. Sanskrit portion, see AI. Ep., No. 51 of 1949-50, App. B.

cells.location: Baroda † — Gujarat

cells.location: Bījāpur — Karnataka
cells.place: Archaeological Museum. Slab in the Museum. No. 5. From a niche in the fort wall, Belgaum.
cells.remarks: States that Ya'qūb 'Alī Khān laid the foundation of the fortwall on a solid and sound basis, the date of whose completion was given in the chronogram.

cells.location: Bījāpur — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 2 †

cells.remarks: After giving a Qur'ānic verse and invoking the blessings of Muḥammad and 'Ali, states that two gardens (and) two ... and... were constructed and endowed with the implication that whoever sets his eye on that will incur the curse of God.

cells.location: Bījāpur — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 3 †
cells.remarks: Records that five shops situated adjacent to each other to the right of Shāh Bāzār, were constructed and endowed during the reign of 'Ali 'Adil Shah I, by the great Khān Jannat Khān for the purpose of defraying the expenses of oil, wax for chandeliers, carpets, etc., of the mosque of Malik Amīna'l Mulk; and also for the salary of a Mu'adhdhin at the rate of one lānka a day and that of the pīsh namāz and farrāsh, six jikāni a day. See also Memoirs of the Archaeological Survey, No. 49, p. 71. Published in op. cit., p. 50.

cells.location: Bījāpur — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 4. From Fath Darwaza †
cells.remarks: Bilingual. The Persian portion is fragmentary and seems to refer to the Qawānīn-i-Hindī (i.e. written agreement in the Indian language) issued by Khān-i-z-am Ghālib Khān. cells.location: Bījāpur — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 5 †

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 10 †

cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 11 †
cells.remarks: Indistinct. Seems to mention Sayyid Afdal, son of Sayyid Husain, sharif(?) inhabitant of Kināna dargāh(?) under Aurangabad. Purport not clear.

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 13. From Dhandurga, Bijapur District. †
cells.remarks: Contains only Nad-'i-'Alī.

cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 14 †
cells.remarks: Ornamental. A few words mostly correlative with the word 'Ilm have been inscribed with a plain circular border in such a way that the elongated strokes of their letters have been interwoven to make a perfect geometrical design in the centre. Purport not clear.

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 15. From Takiya mosque †
cells.remarks: Comprises a part of a verse from the Qur'an ch. IX, verse 108 with illegible letters... Neither the name of the builder nor the purport of the record is mentioned. cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 16 †
cells.remarks: Contains the word Allāh only.

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 17 †
cells.remarks: Purport of the record not clear. Contains two lines: Fath Shāh majālis dār ne ne jamājī majālis dār ne and six words at the corners and top and bottom which are illegible.

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 18 †

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 19 †
cells.remarks: Contains only the words: Faqīr Qādirī Sayyid Mustafā.

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 20, received from the Jagīrdār of Dargah, Bijapur District. †
cells.remarks: Contains the words Allāh, the name of the Prophet, and a chronogram giving the date of the death of his four companions. The last line bearing the date is worn out.

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · BOMBAY—concld. / BIJAPUR DISTRICT—concld. / Bijapur—concld. — Karnataka
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 21, originally from the Fath Mahal. †
cells.remarks: States that Sayyid Shāh Mardān, son of Sayyid Saif-Ullāh endowed for the twelve Imāms, the mosque having two wells, one inside and one outside, and the garden which was his property and purchased by him, having three wells, one each for the mosque, the garden, and the Dargah of the said mosque and also for his sons—Shāh Saif-Ullāh, Shāh Asad-Ullāh and Shāh Lutfullāh, with the condition that its trusteeship would remain with the latters' mother and after her death, with them. No date.

cells.location: Poona — Maharashtra
cells.place: Museum of the Bhārata Itihāsa Samshodhaka Mandala. Slab in the Museum.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and damaged. Could not be made out. From the style of writing it appears to belong to not later than the 14th century A.D.

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · Hazrat Nizamuddin — Karnataka

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · Palam — Karnataka

cells.location: BOMBAY / BIJAPUR DISTRICT · Palam — Karnataka
cells.place: Ghandafā mosque, arch of the central chamber. Southern arch †

cells.location: Gwalior — Madhya Pradesh

cells.location: MADHYA BHARAT / GIRD DISTRICT · MADHYA BHARAT—concld / GIRD DISTRICT—concld / Gwalior—concld — Madhya Pradesh

cells.remarks: States that this step-well was constructed during the reign of Ibrāhīm Shāh, son of Sikandar Shāh, by Malikul-Umarā Fath Muḥammad, son of Kamal Naufil who held the title of Falāhu'l Mulk. Also mentions Sharafu'l Mulk ns the muqti' of the Shiqq of Chanderi.

cells.location: MADHYA BHARAT / GIRD DISTRICT · MADHYA BHARAT—concld / GIRD DISTRICT—concld / Gwalior—concld — Madhya Pradesh
cells.place: Kept in Archaeological Museum. No. 7. From Narwar Fort †

LXXII, verse 18; IX, 108; II, 255, and a tradition of the Prophet) and a poetical fragment stating that during the reign of Muhammad Shah 'Ādil, the monument was constructed by Sayyid Aḥmad, son of Walī Husain and his spiritual guide Nūzīrī Shattārī as the composer and engraver of the record respectively. It also mentions, in the margin, Khān Jalālī, son of Munawwar as the 'āmil.

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / NAGPUR DISTRICT · MADHYA PRADESH / NAGPUR DISTRICT — Maharashtra

'Uthmān.

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / NAGPUR DISTRICT · Damoh — Maharashtra

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / NAGPUR DISTRICT · Damoh — Maharashtra

cells.location: Madras — Tamil Nadu

cells.location: Madras — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Kept in Government Museum. Copper plate in the place of Ghandafā †
cells.date: Jumādī II 1, Regnal year 2=1714 A. D., June 3.
cells.language: Sanskrit verse in Telugu characters; Persian, Nasta‘līq.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. The Persian portion states that on the date mentioned, Todar Mal, alias ('urf) Srī Niwās Dās, son of Teckchand, son of Hans Gopāl, inhabitant of Chakwa Khurd in the pargana of Etāwah, who was the deputy (nāib) of Nawwāb Sa'ādatu'llāh Khān, the dīwān and ṣūbedār of Karnāṭak, came to the pargana of Srī Mushnī in possession of the local zamīndār, and having had the darsan of Vārāh Swāmin made a grant of five villages, viz., Kīlplūvangulī (Kīlpuḷiyaṅguḷi) and others, in accordance with the sanad of the said zamīndār, for the maintenance of the god. It ends with the imprecation that whoever, whether a Hindu or a Muslim, does not abide by this order will be guilty of having deserted his dharma and īmān. (cf. A Catalogue of the Copper-Plate grants in the Madras Museum, p. 41). For the Sanskritic portion, see No. 15 of Appendix A.

cells.location: MADRAS / KURNOOL DISTRICT · Jajpur — Andhra Pradesh

cells.location: MADRAS / KURNOOL DISTRICT · Panipat — Andhra Pradesh

cells.remarks: Fragmentary. The extant portion contains part of the throne Verse (Qurān, ch. II, V. 225) and the words, 'the construction of the mosque of His Majesty, the pole-star of the lesser firmament, Zahīru'd-Dīn Muḥammad Bābur Ghāzī, may his sovereignty endure for ever, and this affair presages.......' cells.location: MADRAS / KURNOOL DISTRICT · Sonepat — Andhra Pradesh

cells.location: MADRAS / KURNOOL DISTRICT · Sonepat † — Andhra Pradesh

cells.location: RAJASTHAN · RAJASTHAN — Rajasthan

cells.location: RAJASTHAN · RAJASTHAN — Rajasthan

cells.remarks: Gives the date of construction of a hammām (bath-house) by Iskandar Isawī. Text composed by Ghubārī.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · BHARATPUR DISTRICT Bharatpur — Rajasthan
cells.place: State Museum. Slab in the Mughal Museum.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that this chabūtra was constructed during the reign of Zaīru’d Dīn Muhammad Bābur and during the governorship of prince Muhammad Kāmrān Bahādur by the royal Amīr Nizāmu’d Dīn, a faithful follower of Islām wa’l Muslimīn, Amīr Khān Muhammad (?).

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda — Rajasthan
cells.place: Slab lying near the tomb called Pīr by the local residents
cells.remarks: Comprises religious texts in Arabic, mostly admonitory. Fragmentary. The text is followed by the words, 'commemoration of the hoped creature Shaikh Mas‘ūd ‘Īsā Afghān' and the date.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda † — Rajasthan
cells.place: Another slab in the place of Qādīzādgān †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to be in continuation of the above epigraph. Contains religious texts intended as sermon and prayers, the latter containing the name of Shaikh Mas‘ūd ‘Īsā Afghān.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda † — Rajasthan
cells.place: A third slab lying near the tomb called Pīr by the local residents, mosque of Qādīzādgān. †
cells.remarks: Records the name Mas‘ūd as the occupant of the grave in one of the verses that follow the traditions of the Prophet and also contains the saying of a saint Khwāja Imām. Ends with the word 'tammat' (end) which indicates that this is probably the concluding portion of the previous epigraphs (Nos. 102-3).

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda † — Rajasthan
cells.place: Cenotaph of a grave in the place of Qādīzādgān †
cells.remarks: Gives the date of death of Shaikh Mas‘ūd ‘Īsā Afghān.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda † — Rajasthan
cells.place: Another grave in the place of Qādīzādgān †
cells.remarks: Gives the date of death of Shaikh Dā’ūd Thābit Afghān.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda † — Rajasthan
cells.place: Jodhpur,-Sardar Museum. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Posal, Nagaur.
cells.language: Persian, Naskh; Sanskrit, Nāgarī †
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Slightly damaged. The Persian version seems to record that his holiness, Shaikhu'i Maghāikh Shaikh Sulaimān got vaected the posāl of Kirst Chand and caused it to be handled over by Masnad-i-Āli Yūsuf Daulat Khan Husain Sūr. Invokes a curse on those who try to violate this order. For the Sanskrit portion, see No. 423-A of Appendix B.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda — Rajasthan
cells.place: Jodhpur,-Sardar Museum. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Posal, Nagaur. No. 2. From Nagaur. †
cells.remarks: Mentions that a well was constructed during the reign of Jalaluddin Muhammad Akbar by the orders of the Danlat Khān, Husain Qulī Khān.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda — Rajasthan
cells.place: Jodhpur,-Sardar Museum. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Posal, Nagaur. No. 3. From a mosque, Nagaur. †
cells.remarks: Assigns the construction of a mosque in the Mahalla Arayārī to Tayyib, son of Shahīdand during the reign of Sultan Shahābuddin Shāh Jahān Ghāzī, during the term of governorship of Nawwab Diler Khān, son of Daryā Khān, Khān-i-Khānān II. The date is that of the writing.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / BHARATPUR DISTRICT · Etamda — Rajasthan
cells.place: Jodhpur,-Sardar Museum. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Posal, Nagaur. No. 4. From Phulclao gate, Jodhpur. †
cells.remarks: States at the auspicious and happy time a voice from Hatif said:- May victory saying that the fort of Islam was glorified by this victory".

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / UDAIPUR DISTRICT · UDAIPUR DISTRICT Udaipur,-Victoria Hall Museum — Rajasthan
cells.place: Slab in the Museum. From near the fort Chitorgarh.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Eulogises Ghiyāsuddin Din Tughluq Shāh and the pivot of the kingdom, Malik Asaduddin Arsalān, the generous. Purport of the record not quite clear. The year and date are lost in the missing portion of the stone.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / UDAIPUR DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA Junagadh — Rajasthan
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Pathanwadi mosque, Patan Sorath, District.
cells.date: A. H. 726, Dhū'l Qa'da=1326 A.D., Sept.-Oct.
cells.remarks: States that this mosque was constructed during the reign of Muhammad Shāh, son of Tughluq Shāh and during the governorship of Tāj-i-Duwal Ahmad by Hamid Ahmad.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / UDAIPUR DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA Junagadh — Rajasthan
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Pathanwadi mosque, Patan Sorath, District. No. 2. From a mosque near the Mota Darwaza, Patan, Sorath. †
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Records the erection of a structure, obviously a mosque, during the reign of Sultan Ahmad I by Fadiullah Ahmad Abū Rajā.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / UDAIPUR DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA Junagadh — Rajasthan
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Pathanwadi mosque, Patan Sorath, District. No. 3. From near the 'Mota Darwaza, Patan. †
cells.remarks: Greatly damaged. Seems to record the removal by the order of the Sultan, of certain inconveniences and harassment of the Sultan on the occasions of marriage.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / UDAIPUR DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA Junagadh — Rajasthan
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Pathanwadi mosque, Patan Sorath, District. No. 4. From the Mota Darwaza, Patan. †
cells.date: A. H. 859, Dhi'I Qa'da 11=1455 A.D., Oct. 13; V.S. I....., Kārtika su
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Damaged and worn out. Seems to contain the purport of a royal decree issued by Sultan Qutbu'd Din Ahmad II enjoining upon the government officials to abstain from any illegal or unjust act as may cause oppression and injustice to the public.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / UDAIPUR DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA Junagadh — Rajasthan
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum, No. 1. From Pathanwadi mosque, Patan Sorath, District. No. 5. From Pushpawada, Sorath District. †
cells.date: A. H. 862, Rabī I 15=1458 A.D., January 31.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. States that during the reign of Sultān Qutbu'd Dīn, son of Muhammad Shāh, this fort (bigār) was constructed by Malik Asad, (son of) Muhammad, (son of) Mubārak Sultānpurī. The Sanskrit version gives the name of the place also—Pushnawada—and refers to the kot, i.e., a fort (cf. Epigraphia Indo-Moslemica, 1935-36, p. 48, pl. XXXV(b) and 1939-40, p. 47, Indian Antiquary, 1879, p. 183). For the Sanskrit portion, see No. 433-A of Appendix B.

cells.location: SAURASHTRA / SORATH DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA—concld. / SORATH DISTRICT—concld. / Junagarh—concld. — Gujarat
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum. No. 6. From Patan.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the erection of a mosque. Name of the builder and the date are not clear.

cells.location: SAURASHTRA / SORATH DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA—concld. / SORATH DISTRICT—concld. / Junagarh—concld. — Gujarat
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum, No. 6. From Pâtan. No. 7. From the Market square, Mughal Patan. †
cells.remarks: Weather-beaten. Contains an order issued by Shah Wardi Khân, the governor of Sorath, stating that he would cut off the hands of the merchant, if the latter, contrary to the previous governors and officials, of compelling the merchants to purchase the product of their land in lots and levy other imposts which resulted in loss to the latter. Ends with a warning against the continuance of that practice in future.

cells.location: SAURASHTRA / SORATH DISTRICT · SAURASHTRA—concld. / SORATH DISTRICT—concld. / Junagarh—concld. — Gujarat
cells.place: Museum of Antiquities. Slab in the Museum, No. 6. From Pâtan. No. 8. From Patan †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and damaged. Most of the letters have peeled off. Part of the record is number. Contains a prayer to request the reader to invoke prayers for the builder, viz. one who was inspired by Divine guidance, the mean slave, Mubārak, the bearer of the Quran.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT · UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT Agra — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Reri Fort. Top of the Ghazani Ghaznavid Gate.
cells.remarks: Undated. Invokes blessings on Sultan Mahmud, son of Sabuktigin.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT · UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT Agra — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Reri Fort. Top of the Ghazani Ghaznavid Gate. East wall of the guard room, Delhi Gate. †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. The extant piece bears the words nuzūl-i-ijlāl fasmūd (see also, Transactions of the Archaeological Society of Agra, 1874, p. xx).

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT · UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT Agra — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Reri Fort. Top of the Ghazani Ghaznavid Gate. Below the above †
cells.remarks: Records Jahangir's accession to the throne. Composed and written by Muhammad Ma'sum al-Bakkari.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT · UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT Agra — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Reri Fort. Top of the Ghazani Ghaznavid Gate. Four sides of the Black Throne †
cells.remarks: Describes the throne and eulogizes Jahangir both as prince Salim and emperor.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT · UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT Agra — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Reri Fort. Top of the Ghazani Ghaznavid Gate. On the Hasti-i-Jahangiri †
cells.remarks: Badly damaged. Only a few words can be made out. Mentions the name of Jahangir and the laud-i-Jahangiri. The date is given in the chronogram contained in the last verse.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT · UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT Agra — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Reri Fort. Top of the Ghazani Ghaznavid Gate. Slab fixed on the edge of the northern rampart †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and damaged. The extant portion seems to refer to (the construction of) a mosque in the capital.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH AGRA DISTRICT · Fahtepur Sikri — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab built into a well
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a well during the reign of the emperor Zahiru'd-Din Muhammad Babur at the time of his return from his battle with Rāna Sänga.

cells.location: ALIGARH DISTRICT · ALIGARH DISTRICT Aligarh — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab built into the wall of an orchard near Qāzi Khān's tomb.
cells.date: A. H. 970, Ramadan = 1563 A.D., April- May.
cells.remarks: Published in the Epigraphia Indo-Moslemica, 1925-26, p. 8, Plate V(a).

cells.location: ALIGARH DISTRICT · ALIGARH DISTRICT Aligarh † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab built into the mosque of Dullalı Khān
cells.remarks: States that these buildings (mosque and tomb) were built by Dullali Khān, son of Darya Khân. The date is given by a chronogram.

cells.location: ALIGARH DISTRICT · ALIGARH DISTRICT Aligarh † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab fixed in the Masjid-i-Bazar
cells.remarks: Gives a short account of the reconstruction of the mosque originally constructed by Khwaja Basant, khwajasarā of Nawwab Thabit Khan through the efforts of Mr Saidul Din of Narnaul and of the purchase of shops adjoining it and establishment of an endowment, for their maintenance. It is stated that at the request of Haji Hafiz Muhammad Ishaq was made the trustee (mutawalli) of the mosque.

cells.location: ALIGARH DISTRICT · Pilakhna — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Northern entrance of the Jami Masjid.
cells.language: Arabic prose and Persian verse, Naskh.
cells.remarks: States that the mosque was constructed during the reign of Zahiru'd-Din Muhammad Babur Ghāzī by Ashrafa'l Ashrāf Ghūran, son of Muhammad, son of Islam.

cells.location: ETAH DISTRICT · ETAH DISTRICT Sakit — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab from a ruined Imambara inside the so-called Sakit Fort.
cells.remarks: States that 'the Almāsgāh was constructed.' The text forms the chronogram.

cells.location: ETAH DISTRICT · ETAH DISTRICT Sakit † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab built into the west wall of the mosque near the above Imāmbāra.
cells.date: A. H. 970, Sha'bān =1563 A.D., March- April.
cells.remarks: Partly damaged. States that in the reign of the great king, the exalted, Khaqan, lord of the kings of Arabia and 'Ajam, preserver of the cities of God and helper of His creatures, the support of the kingdom of Hijaz and Yemen, Du'l- Sultan Mahmud Akbar Bādshāh Ghāzī, Khān Di Ibrahim Khan constructed this noble and blessed mosque. The names of superintendents or architects have peeled off while that of the scribe is Ismail.

cells.location: ETAH DISTRICT · ETAH DISTRICT Sakit — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab built into the west wall of the mosque near the above Imāmbāra. Slab built into the well o another sūr mosque. †
cells.remarks: States that during the reign of the king of the world, Faridu'd- Dunya wa'd Din Abu'l Muzaffar Sher Shah 'Adil, Mas'ud Khan, son of Misa'il Khān Batani (?) constructed this anonymous mosque.

cells.location: ETAWAH DISTRICT · ETAWAH DISTRICT Ekdil — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab above the doorway of the mosque of Vakil Khān.
cells.remarks: Assigns the construction of a mosque to Vakil Khān built under the superintendence of Bihikān Khān during Shah Jahān's reign. Name of the scribe is Muhammad.

cells.location: ETAWAH DISTRICT · ETAWAH DISTRICT Ekdil † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab above the main gate of the town
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions the foundation of the town, which was named Sarai Vakil, during the reign of Shah Jahan. The builder is obviously the same as the one mentioned in the preceding paragraph. The chronogram bearing the date is not quite clear.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / FYZABAD DISTRICT · UTTAR PRADESH—contd. / FYZABAD DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Ayodhya.—Pulpit in the Bāburi mosque
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the mosque by Amir Bāqī at the instance of emperor Bābur.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / FYZABAD DISTRICT · Ayodhya † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Central entrance to the prayer chamber, same place.
cells.remarks: States that during the reign of Bābur qalandar, who conquered the earth as the sky does, one of his great nobles, the second Asaf, Amir Bāqī, whose policy is the counsellor of the kingdom, built this mosque and fort. Ended his prayer for the builder. Written by Fathullah Muhammad Gīlānī.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / FYZABAD DISTRICT · Mohoba — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Tughluq's mosque. Over the eastern doorway.
cells.remarks: States that during the reign of the king of seven climes, Ghiyāsud-Dīn wa'd Dunyā Tughluq Shāh who, like Alexander, conquered cities and towns of India, this mosque at Mohoba was completed with Malik Tājud-Dīn Ahmad was the governor and that the door, walls and the courtyard of the mosque were also made up-to-date. The date is that of completion.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / FYZABAD DISTRICT · Kalbi — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Tomb of Shāh Abul Fath, Mahalla Harīganj.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the tomb of Shaikh Bāhā Hājī Samad begun in A. H. 853, Shāh-bān, and completed seven months later.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / FYZABAD DISTRICT · Kalbi † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Tomb of Shaikh Bāhā Hājī Samad, Mughal. Near Thatheron kī Ku'in, Mahalla Udal Sarāī. Over the eastern entrance.
cells.remarks: States that this dome (for tomb) of Shaikh Bāhā Hājī Samad was built during the reign of the Mughal king Bābur and the governorship of Sultān 'Alam Lodī.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / FYZABAD DISTRICT · Kalbi † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Head-stone of a grave near the Hospital Post Office.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Most of the letters broken. Contains a fragment of verses invoking God's pardon through the blessings of the twelve Imāms. The chronogram containing date, given also in figures, has worn out. Appears to be an epitaph.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT · JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Jaunpur.—Tomb of Sulaimān Shāh in Jail compound.
cells.date: A. H. 1199, Muharram 21, Regnal year 26=1784 A.D., December 4.
cells.remarks: Records the death of Mubārak 'Alī Khān, a Sayyid.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT · JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Jaunpur.—Tomb of Sulaimān Shāh in Jail compound.
cells.remarks: Published in the Epigraphia Indo-Moslemica, 1937-38, p. 40, Pl. XIII(a).

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT · JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Jaunpur.—Tomb of Sulaimān Shāh in Jail compound.
cells.remarks: Ibid., Pl. XII(c).

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.remarks: Ibid. [Epigraphia Indo-Moslemica, 1937-38], p. 41, Pl. XIII(c).

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.language: Arabic and Persian, Thulth and Nasta‘liq
cells.remarks: Much damaged. About half of the epigraph totally gone. Seems to record the repairs of public roads and thoroughfares carried out at the order of the King. ‘Alī Shāh is the title of ‘Alī Shāh of Audh. Also mentions Qutb-ud-Daulah Mu‘azzam-ul-Mulk ‘Alī Tajallī Bahādur Haibat Jang.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.remarks: States that 12 lac dams along with jewels, pearls and two thousand gold mohurs were kept in the underground chamber in the Sāhī Masjid by (?) Sayyid Husain Fīrūz. Name of the king not mentioned. Probably late Mughal period.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.remarks: Constitutes a table showing distances in kosha between important cities and towns of India, with a few lines on the top giving the method of reference.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Kept in Provincial Museum. No. 5. †
cells.remarks: Another tabular chart giving the same kind of information as above.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. The extant portion contains only the name of the great Khān and Khānān, master of the sword and pen, champion of the age and time, Ulugh Khān. Purport of the record not clear.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.remarks: Bodily damaged. Seems to record the excavation of a tank. Begins with Bismillah and Throne Verse (Qurān, ch. II, verse 255).

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Mughal
cells.remarks: Bodily damaged. Records the construction of an auspicious structure by one Iskandar. The composer of the Persian verse is unknown. (For the Sanskrit portion, see no. 541 of Appendix B.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / JAUNPUR DISTRICT · JAUNPUR DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Mughal
cells.remarks: States that when the compendium of excellence and perfection, elevator of the banners of kingdoms and nations, etc., viz., the Jām-like king Muhammad Bābur, lighted the torch of fortune in India, Sambhal was chosen as the place for the construction of this mosque, the best of the pillars of the state, to construct this mosque which might remain free from damage and ruin. It was completed on the first of Rabī‘ I. The words giving the day and month form the chronogram.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / MURADABAD DISTRICT · MURADABAD DISTRICT—concld. / Sambhal—concld. — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Another slab in the place of Bābur †
cells.remarks: States that the king of the domain of generosity, Sayyid Qutb carried out repairs to the old mosque.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / MURADABAD DISTRICT · MURADABAD DISTRICT—concld. / Sambhal—concld. † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab fixed to the left mihrāb in the place of Bābur. †
cells.remarks: States that the repairs to the Jāmi ‘mosque, which had fallen down on all sides, were ordered to be carried out by the good natured Rustam Khān, the brave, the religious and the victorious. The work was supervised by one ‘Abdus Salām. It gives three chronograms for date of repairs, one of which is composed by As‘adī and another by Kamāl.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / MURADABAD DISTRICT · MURADABAD DISTRICT—concld. / Sambhal—concld. † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Tojā Mainī’s grave. On the side
cells.remarks: Worn out. Contains Nūd-al-All and the name Bābā Khān (or Bābā Jān).

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / MURADABAD DISTRICT · MURADABAD DISTRICT—concld. / Sambhal—concld. — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Tojā Mainī’s grave. On the side. On the headstone †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Bears the date only.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / MURADABAD DISTRICT · MURADABAD DISTRICT—concld. / Sambhal—concld. † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab built into the Sūrī Tārīn mosque
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. States that this mosque was constructed at the auspicious time by Miyān Dīdh, son of Mughulū (?) of the tribe of Tārīn, in the reign of the king of kings, Sultān Sikandar, son of Buhlūl Shāh.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / VINDHYA DISTRICT / TIKAMGARH DISTRICT · VINDHYA DISTRICT / TIKAMGARH DISTRICT — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Jatara.—Slab fixed into the Laulibagron kī Bāolī.
cells.date:
A. H. 839. Sha'bān 6. Thursday—1436
A.D., February 24
(which was Friday).
cells.remarks: Records that the completion of this step-well was constructed by Dīn I-mīl Khān, son of Nizām Khān. The builder was Bhola Mahārāj, the wine seller, an inhabitant of the town of Jatara.

cells.location: UTTAR PRADESH / VINDHYA DISTRICT / TIKAMGARH DISTRICT · VINDHYA DISTRICT / TIKAMGARH DISTRICT † — Uttar Pradesh
cells.place: Slab fixed into the Shāhkhān kī Bāolī in Jamlatpura.
cells.date: A.H. 906, Rajab, Wednesday, V.S. 1557, Phālgun-sudi 3=1501 A.D., Feb.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Records that this step-well was constructed by Shivan Kunwar Kāliwānī, a resident of the town of Jatara, during the period of Khān-i-A‘zam and Khān-i-Mu‘zzam Tātār Khān, son of Muhammad Khān. For the Sanskrit portion, see No. 566-A of Appendix B.
